subject: Money
title: Bubbles as Progress
description: A quick, practical guide to Bubbles as Progress.

hook.text: The dot-com bubble wasted billions but funded the fiber optic cables that power today's internet.

buildup.text: Economist Carlota Perez argues every technological revolution follows the same cycle: bubble, crash, deployment.

discovery.text: Bubbles overfund new technology. The excess capital builds infrastructure that wouldn't exist under rational investment.

twist.text: Railway mania, canal mania, electrification, the internet—each destroyed fortunes but left lasting infrastructure.

climax.text: Bubbles are painful but productive. The question isn't whether they happen—it's how to distribute the pain fairly.

punchline.text: Bubbles build the future. On other people's money.

quiz.question: According to Carlota Perez, what useful role do bubbles play?
options: They overfund technology, creating infrastructure that outlasts the crash
